validity.recommendation: Treat P1841 as unverified/low-confidence; find one independent source that actually NAMES a Baiji→K3→Al-Qa'im gas transmission line before keeping it green. If none exists, consider merging into general North Gas Company context or flagging for possible removal.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's OWN support for this row is two OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletins (ASB 2012 p.75; ASB 2017) — aggregate national-statistics documents that report country-level pipeline totals, NOT a source that names a 'Baiji-K3-Al Kaem gas pipeline' or gives its route/length/diameter/capacity. So the cited source does not corroborate the specific pipeline. Independent searching (EN + AR: Iraqi press, North Gas Company, oil ministry, MEED, EIA, USGS mineral yearbooks, FAS/globalsecurity Al-Qaim files) surfaced NO independent source that names this pipeline or gives any of its specs. Every apparent web 'confirmation' of a 'Baiji-K3-Al Qaim gas pipeline' traces straight back to gem.wiki (circular). The underlying physical premise is partly plausible — the Al-Qa'im fertilizer/phosphate complex (real; FAS: 380 km WNW of Baghdad, 34°22'N 41°07'E; produced ammonia 1984–1990s using natural-gas feedstock) was historically gas-supplied via North Gas Company (Kirkuk associated gas processed and moved via Baiji), so a Baiji→Al-Qa'im gas corridor is physically conceivable. But I could not independently document it as a discrete, named, operating transmission line. Classification note: the name uses OIL-pipeline station nomenclature (K2=Baiji, K3=Haditha pump station) and a 16-inch diameter identical to the crude 'Baiji-Hadithah' (16", 84 mi) and 'Iraq-Jordan' (K3→Tarbil, 16", 219 mi) lines in the GulfPub oil roster — raising the possibility this 'gas' row was constructed from oil-corridor station names. Duplicate check: NOT the same as P2231 'North Gas-Baiji' (→Saladin, 145 km, 24") nor P4401 'Okaz/Akkas' (Anbar, 30 km, 16"); no other roster row runs Baiji→Al-Qa'im, so no in-roster duplicate found. Net: existence is weakly supported at best; sole citation is aggregate and does not name the line.

validity.recommendation: Do not trust Capacity=2.41 MMcf/d or Length=431 km without an independent source. Both are unverified and physically doubtful; leave flagged rather than green.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity 2.41 MMcf/d is physically implausible for a 431 km, 16-inch trunk line feeding a fertilizer/ammonia complex — a 16" line moves on the order of ~100+ MMcf/d, and an Al-Qa'im-scale ammonia plant would need tens of MMcf/d, not ~2.4. This tiny value is part of a suspicious cluster of sub-3 MMcf/d 'capacities' across the Iraq gas operating roster (P1845 2.00, P1846 0.67, P1847 0.70, P1848 2.10, P2231 0.89) that look like a systematic data artifact rather than real throughput. Length 431 km is also unverified and looks overstated: Baiji (≈34.93N,43.49E) → Haditha/K3 (≈34.07N,42.38E) → Al-Qa'im (≈34.37N,41.12E) is only ~250–260 km along a routed corridor, so 431 km is ~1.7x the plausible routed distance. No independent source AGREES with the GEM capacity, length, or 16" diameter — they are uncorroborated. Not silently passing.

waypoints.name: Haditha / K3 pumping station area (Euphrates valley)

routes.corridor_desc: Inferred corridor (NOT from a route source): from Baiji (Saladin) southwest to the Haditha/K3 pump-station area on the Euphrates, then northwest up the Euphrates valley through Anbar to the Al-Qa'im fertilizer complex near the town of Al-Qa'im on the Syrian border. Endpoints are named and defensible (Baiji and Haditha are well-known towns; the Al-Qa'im complex coordinate 34°22'N 41°07'E is from FAS → ~34.37N,41.12E). The 'K3' waypoint follows the pipeline name and the oil-corridor station convention, not an independent gas-route source, so the actual alignment is unknown and the bound is loose. Routed length ~250–260 km vs the sheet's 431 km — do not treat the corridor as authoritative.
routes.researcher_notes: End coordinate (Al-Qa'im complex) sourced from FAS (34°22'N 41°07'E, verified 200 + tokens 'Al Qaim'/'380'). Baiji and Haditha coordinates are defensible from those named towns' well-known locations, not invented. No independent source documents the actual pipe alignment, and existence itself is doubtful, so this is a loosely-bounded suggestion only — never auto-apply. No coordinate was fabricated.

summary: P1841 concern (existence + spec): sole citation is aggregate OPEC ASB that doesn't name the line; no independent source confirms a Baiji→K3→Al-Qa'im gas pipeline; capacity 2.41 MMcf/d and length 431 km physically implausible/uncorroborated; loose inferred corridor Baiji→Haditha(K3)→Al-Qa'im, suggested route accuracy low.
